minutes.headline: Board heard the FY21 preliminary town budget and ADA transition plan; ratified a reserve officer; went to executive session
minutes.summary: The board ratified a reserve police officer appointment, heard an ADA rights-of-way transition plan, and received the town manager's FY21 preliminary budget presentation. Residents raised a collective bargaining funding concern, school funding and board conduct. Marijuana ballot questions were put on next week's agenda, and the board entered executive session on collective bargaining.

what_happened.line: The Select Board heard the town manager's FY21 preliminary budget, which leaves an unallocated balance and does not meet the superintendent's request.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a reserve police officer.
Consultants presented an ADA rights-of-way transition plan recommending a five-year ramp plan and a yearly amount for removing sidewalk barriers.
The budget presentation said free cash goes to capital, OPEB and stabilization rather than the operating budget, and that the tax rate is projected to rise slightly.
The board put marijuana warrant articles and ballot questions on next week's agenda, then moved to enter executive session on collective bargaining.

why_it_matters: The preliminary FY21 budget points to a slightly higher tax rate and a school budget below what the superintendent asked for, both of which residents may be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.

The ADA plan would set a multi-year cost for ramps and sidewalks that competes with other capital needs, and the open collective bargaining question for patrol officers could affect future payroll costs.
